doc.name: A — running shoes catalogue, editorial shadow play, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: carbon-plate racing shoe
Category: running shoes
Shot programme: editorial shadow play
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are a commercial stills director briefing a running shoes capture. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the open and in-use in an editorial shadow play treatment.

SUBJECT. A carbon-plate racing shoe. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Cap off, lid open or mechanism deployed, mid-use state. Shoot on a 200mm compression telephoto at f/2, framing for dead-centre symmetry with mirrored negative space.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a beauty dish above the lens axis with a silver reflector under the chin. Stage the product on or against matte acrylic, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a desaturated Nordic palette with cold blue shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.
